title: Verifier‑Grounded NetConfig‑Semantic Study: A Preregistered Paired Test of paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (shared_initial_candidate)
abstract: Estimand (preregistered): paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline evaluated under shared_initial_candidate semantics. We preregistered and executed CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1 comparing a deterministic template baseline to a single‑pass LLM generator (declared_model_version = gpt‑5‑mini) on N = 120 synthetic intent→configuration tasks using a deterministic validator. Under the frozen confirmatory semantics (one canonical candidate reused per pair) both conditions passed the verifier on all tasks (baseline = 120/120; guarded = 120/120). Paired difference = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. We publish the full execution and analysis artifacts (see execution/execution_manifest.json in the bundle) and diagnose—on the basis of archived traces—why the preregistered shared_initial_candidate design produced a degenerate paired contingency (identical canonical candidates + deterministic validator). We provide artifact‑grounded, runnable modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed confirmatory design, validator diversification, expanded task heterogeneity) that preserve reproducibility while answering the operational question practitioners typically need: the independent per‑condition generative reliability of LLM outputs under verifier checks.

sections.introduction: Translating operator intent into device configuration is a safety‑critical NetOps task: incorrect command sequences can break reachability, violate ACLs, or create unsafe transients during multi‑step changes. We preregistered CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1 to evaluate a concrete estimand: the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under shared_initial_candidate semantics (see preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37). The study couples LLM generation to a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) so correctness is auditable. Our deliverables are (1) exhaustive, byte‑traceable artifacts enabling exact reruns, (2) preregistered confirmatory inference (N = 120 paired tasks), and (3) an artifact‑grounded diagnosis and immediately runnable protocol adjustments that answer the operational reliability question practitioners actually need. All execution artifacts and SHA‑256 fingerprints are published in the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json). Representative canonical candidate files that were reused across paired episodes include execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 8f38c8becd7e1e36...), task-000002 (SHA‑256 ae967f70dfb6ccb8...), and task-000003 (SHA‑256 f7f4db249ecbbce...).
sections.related_work: Verifier‑grounded evaluation is standard practice for pre‑deployment NetOps checks: tools such as Batfish and Batfish‑lineage research provide deterministic reachability and ACL analyses and have been widely adopted for verifying configuration artifacts [Brown et al., 2023; DOI:10.1145/3603269.3604866]. Recent LLM→NetOps work explores intent→config generation, generate–validate–repair loops, and bounded iterative repairs; methodological axes that vary across studies include sampling semantics (single canonical candidate vs independent sampling), repair budgets, and validator scope (syntactic vs full semantic validators). Surveys and recent studies emphasize that repair‑loop orchestration and validator feedback design often dominate final repair effectiveness, and that most repair gains occur in the first few iterations. Our contribution is not a new verifier or model but a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored experiment that makes explicit how generation semantics interact with deterministic validators to produce confirmatory inferences.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen design. The study preregistration (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; SHA‑256 7db1663cf3...) fixed: N = 120 paired tasks (40 per topology class), model = gpt‑5‑mini (declared_model_version; execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e2...), validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, and primary analysis = paired_binary_analysis_v1 (bootstrap 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Task generation. Tasks were programmatically synthesized from deterministic templates (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) that embed initial_state, required_sequence, workflow_policies (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields, minimum_active_in_groups), and expected_final_state. Each task manifest entry and its canonical reference answer are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl and execution/responses/*. We used a single canonical LLM candidate per task and reused it for both baseline and guarded scoring episodes (files execution/responses/task-0000NN-shared-initial.txt; manifest contains per‑file SHA‑256s). Deterministic validation and scoring. The validator enforces transient and final constraints, normalizes commands, and emits a comprehensive JSON trace for each scored episode (execution/scoring/*.json). The scoring rule for the confirmatory test was full_intent_constraint_validation (binary pass = 1). Analysis. The primary estimator is the paired mean of guarded_i − baseline_i across i=1..120. We computed a 95% bootstrap percentile CI with 10,000 resamples (seed = 1729) and exact McNemar two‑sided test on the 2×2 paired table. Mapping required by reviewers (operational question vs preregistered estimand vs cause of degeneracy). See the concise, artifact‑grounded mapping below (references point to archived artifacts): Mapping (a) Practitioner operational question: "What is the independent per‑condition probability that an LLM sample satisfies the verifier?" — requires independent_per_condition sampling (not shared canonical candidates). (b) Preregistered estimand actually tested here: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under shared_initial_candidate semantics (explicit in preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663c...). (c) Why the confirmatory contingency is degenerate (artifact‑visible cause): identical canonical candidate files were reused per pair (execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt; e.g., SHA‑256 8f38c8becd7e1e36...) and the validator is deterministic (execution/scoring/* JSON traces), therefore identical inputs produce identical pass/fail outputs and n_11 = 120. This mapping is supported by the archived paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 9f25790c...) and condition summary (analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256 9c77c96f...).
sections.results: Confirmatory counts and preregistered inference. All preregistered confirmatory episodes completed and are archived. Observed counts: baseline_success_count = 120/120; guarded_success_count = 120/120; complete_pair_count = 120. Paired contingency: n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 9f25790c...). Primary estimand = mean(guarded_i − baseline_i) = 0.00. Bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.00]. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Representative validator traces. Each scored episode emits a validator JSON that records normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, transient checks, and final_state. Example archived traces: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 0d56c1add7c5a57f...), execution/scoring/task-000002-guarded.json (SHA‑256 993b8eb3...), execution/scoring/task-000003-guarded.json (SHA‑256 dad1cf4c...). These show that canonical candidates satisfied task‑encoded required_sequences and workflow_policies for the sampled tasks. Execution accounting. Planned episodes = 240; completed = 240; model_calls_used = 120 (shared_initial generation counted once per pair); failed episodes = 0. All runtime artifacts and provider traces are published (execution/provider_calls/*.json, execution/call_cache/*) to permit deterministic replay and contamination analysis.
sections.discussion: What the confirmatory outcome means. The confirmatory statistics correctly answer the preregistered estimand—whether a deterministic validator treats identical canonical candidates differently across two scoring labels—result: no difference. They do not estimate the independent generative reliability practitioners typically need (the probability that independently sampled LLM outputs pass a verifier). Why the design produced a degenerate contingency. The artifact chain demonstrates the causal mechanism: (1) the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics generated a single canonical candidate per task (execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt), and (2) the deterministic validator deterministically scored that identical candidate for both conditions (execution/scoring/*.json). By design identical artifacts yield identical verifier outputs, producing n_11 = 120. Runnable, artifact‑grounded next steps. The archived pipeline supports deterministic reruns that answer the operational question without inventing new artifacts: (A) independent_per_condition rerun: generate one seed per condition per task and rescore (routes in the manifest permit deterministic replay); (B) multi‑seed design: K ≥ 3 independent seeds per condition per task to estimate per‑condition pass probabilities with bootstrap CIs; (C) validator diversification: add an independent validator and report intersection/union pass rates. Because every file and hash is archived (execution/execution_manifest.json), these reruns are auditable and deterministic. Threats to validity (artifact‑identified). Internal: shared_initial design removed generation variance and hence precluded testing independent generative reliability. Construct: template‑aligned tasks + single validator can overstate success for canonical candidates. External: single model (gpt‑5‑mini) and synthetic tasks limit generalization. Conclusion: transparent preregistration and exhaustive artifact publication make interpretive boundaries explicit and enable immediate remedial reruns.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired experiment and released the exhaustive execution and analysis bundle required for byte‑for‑byte reproduction (execution/execution_manifest.json; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663c...). Under the frozen shared_initial_candidate confirmatory semantics both baseline and gpt‑5‑mini guarded conditions passed the deterministic validator on all N = 120 tasks (both 120/120). Archived traces show that identical canonical candidates and a deterministic validator caused the degenerate paired contingency; thus the confirmatory result does not answer the independent per‑condition generative reliability question. We publish runnable, artifact‑grounded modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed replication, validator diversification) that convert the run into an informative operational comparison while preserving reproducibility. All execution artifacts, provider traces, per‑episode validator JSONs, and SHA‑256 fingerprints are included in the submission bundle to permit exact audit and deterministic reruns.

limitations: Controlled synthetic tasks: programmatic templates produced narrow required_sequences and workflow_policies that favour canonical solutions and limit external generalizability to heterogeneous operational intents.

Confirmatory shared_initial semantics: the preregistered generation_semantics = 'shared_initial_candidate' supplied identical canonical candidates to both conditions per pair, reducing independence between conditions and causing the degenerate paired outcome.

Single canonical seed for confirmatory test: the primary analysis used one canonical seed per task; preregistered exploratory multi‑seed analyses (seeds_1..4) were not included in the confirmatory inference reported here.

Validator–task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces constraints encoded in the task templates, which can increase pass rates for template‑aligned candidates and reduce construct validity for open distributions.

Possible training‑data exposure: preregistered contamination heuristics found no flags under chosen thresholds, but absence of a flag is not proof of zero exposure to related artifacts in model pretraining.

Single‑model, single‑validator run: results apply only to gpt‑5‑mini under the recorded configuration and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; they do not generalize across model families, agentic pipelines, or other validators.
